diagnostics.message: aws_cloudfront_distribution.default has `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket.origin]`, but the distribution already depends on the origin bucket implicitly: its `origin` block sets `domain_name = local.bucket_domain_name`, which resolves through locals (`local.origin_bucket` → `local.origin_bucket_options.new = aws_s3_bucket.origin[0]`) to `aws_s3_bucket.origin.bucket_regional_domain_name`. Terraform therefore already orders the distribution after the bucket, so the explicit depends_on duplicates an existing dependency. It is not visible in the mechanical graph only because it is routed through locals.

aws_cloudfront_distribution.default serves content via the CloudFront origin access identity, whose GetObject/ListBucket permissions are granted by aws_s3_bucket_policy.default (the combined policy document). Nothing in the distribution references the bucket policy and there is no depends_on, so CloudFront can be created/deployed and begin serving before the OAI grant is in place, yielding 403 responses. Add an explicit `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.default]` (a bare depends_on is required here since the policy exposes no attribute the distribution's origin block could reference).
